sources.title: J. S. Milne, Modular Functions and Modular Forms
sources.locator: Ch. 3 Elliptic Functions, printed pp. 41–47 (PDF pp. 41–47); complete chapter argument and named results 3.1–3.13 read, with §3.12 proof limitation noted.

contents.name: Lattices and bases: oriented basis criterion
Quotients of C by lattices: quotient atlas and compact torus
Doubly periodic functions: definition
Proposition 3.1(a)–(b): zero/pole and residue laws
Proposition 3.1(c): Abel sum of a principal divisor
contents.reason: The group-valued principal-divisor condition and its converse belong with the planned divisor and Riemann–Roch treatment, beyond the A-page analytic laws.

contents.name: Corollary 3.2: nonconstant elliptic functions have at least two poles
contents.support: The residue sum excludes a sole simple pole after the pole-free case is excluded by Liouville.

contents.name: Proposition 3.3 and Corollaries 3.4–3.5: torus homomorphisms and isomorphism classes
contents.reason: Classification of homothetic lattices and unmarked tori is reserved for the planned j-invariant page; the quotient construction here needs no classification.

contents.name: Corollary 3.6: complex multiplication of torus endomorphisms
contents.reason: Arithmetic complex multiplication is expressly outside this analytic elliptic-function pair and needs number-theoretic field and order theory.

contents.name: Lemma 3.7 and Weierstrass ℘ construction
Theorem 3.8: prescribed elliptic zero and pole divisors
contents.reason: Existence for arbitrary degree-zero divisors with Abel-sum condition belongs to the later divisor and Riemann–Roch page, not the basic field generators.

contents.name: Proposition 3.9: addition formula
Proposition 3.10: convergence of lattice Eisenstein sums
contents.support: Absolute convergence of G₄ and G₆ gives well-defined g₂ and g₃; the modular cusp limit is not used.

contents.name: Proposition 3.11: elliptic function field and cubic differential relation
Proposition 3.12 first assertion: lattice cubic and torus isomorphism
contents.support: Our proof supplies the nonzero-discriminant and infinity-chart arguments explicitly; Milne abbreviates this assertion and uses later modular theory for the converse.

contents.name: Proposition 3.12 continuation: the addition formula makes uniformization a group homomorphism
contents.support: The new A theorem transports addition through the fixed-lattice biholomorphism and proves directly from the analytic addition identity that the chord-tangent construction is that transported law.

contents.name: Proposition 3.12 converse and Proposition 3.13: all elliptic curves and category equivalences
contents.reason: The converse for arbitrary smooth complex cubics and classification of genus-one marked surfaces require j/moduli or Riemann–Roch beyond the fixed-lattice isomorphism.

sources.title: C. T. McMullen, Advanced Complex Analysis, Math 213a course notes
sources.locator: Ch. 5 §5.1 Doubly-periodic functions, printed pp. 79–90 (PDF pp. 80–91); complete relevant argument, Theorems 5.1–5.21 and corollaries read.

contents.name: §5.1 lattice, torus and doubly periodic functions
Theorem 5.1: ℘ is doubly periodic
Theorem 5.2: fixed-lattice cubic uniformization
Theorem 5.3: printed coordinate-ring expression for the function field
contents.support: As printed, C[x,y]/(F) is an affine coordinate ring, not a field. We use the corrected rational function field formulation in Theorem 5.15 and prove it locally.

contents.name: Basic properties (1)–(2): residue and divisor counts
Basic property (3): Abel sum of zeros and poles
contents.reason: The Abel-sum condition for principal divisors is part of the planned divisor/Riemann–Roch theory; no current theorem consumes it.

contents.name: Theorem 5.4 and Corollary 5.5: cubic factorization and degree-two quotient
contents.support: The degree-two map and three distinct finite branch values are proved before inferring the discriminant.

contents.name: Corollary 5.6: bijection onto the smooth cubic
Theorem 5.7: dimensions of elliptic functions with bounded poles
contents.reason: The full dimension formula is a genus-one Riemann–Roch instance; the present field proof needs only the explicit degree-two ℘ map.

contents.name: Theorem 5.8 and Corollary 5.9: Laurent coefficients and cubic identity
Corollary 5.10: sum of the half-period values
contents.support: The cubic coefficient and distinct-half-period calculation give the root sum zero within the discriminant proof.

contents.name: Alternative one-direction trigonometric sums and G₁
contents.reason: These basis-dependent constructions and the quasimodular G₁ correction are auxiliary to the canonical ℘ theory; modular transformation theory belongs to another page.

contents.name: Theorems 5.11–5.14: rectangular real mapping, inverse elliptic integral and periods
contents.reason: The plan's companion-page harvest explicitly promises the rectangular real mapping, inverse elliptic integral, and period evaluations.
contents.support: The new B example records the reality locus, conformal rectangle, inverse integral and half-period integral formulas.

contents.name: Theorem 5.15: K(E)=C(℘,℘′)
Theorem 5.16 and Corollaries 5.17–5.20: line-cubic sum, negation, chord/tangent and duplication construction
contents.support: The new A item proves the full line-divisor sum and chord law with tangent, vertical and infinity cases. The B duplication computation remains supported by the local analytic addition formula.

contents.name: Sigma product and quasi-period construction
Theorem 5.21: degree-zero divisor is principal iff Abel sum vanishes
contents.reason: The full principal-divisor criterion and existence half belong to the planned compact-surface divisor treatment.

contents.name: §5.2, Theorem 5.16 and Corollaries 5.17–5.20: cubic addition and chord/tangent construction
contents.support: The new A item proves that the geometric chord-tangent law agrees with the transported torus law, with all intersection multiplicities and exceptional projective lines stated.

contents.name: §5.3, Theorems 5.21–5.25: rectangular real locus, inverse integral and periods
contents.support: The new B example records the rectangular reality locus, conformal map, inverse elliptic integral and the real period integrals.

contents.name: §5.4, Theorems 5.26–5.27: cotangent uniformization and the conic
contents.support: The new B example identifies C/Z with the projective conic minus its two omitted finite points, extends the map at the cotangent pole, and proves the differential identity.
